items.title: Type-A Hecke permutation modules: semistandard Murphy bases and Specht filtrations
items.statement:
For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary
finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the
permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type
$\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape. It has a Specht
filtration with multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$ of the
ordinary Specht module $S^\lambda$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). The row-double-coset
membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over
the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the
$\rho$-row parabolic in $S^\lambda$. Moreover the explicit ordinary Garnir
row-coset identity, the additive nonstandard-tableau factorization and the
same-column generator refinement
$$T_am_{st}\equiv-m_{st}+\sum_{u\lhd s}c_um_{ut}\pmod{\text{higher shapes}}$$
hold; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape
terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved
ordinary Murphy dominance ideals
([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]],
[[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]); the finite Garnir
algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that
dominance refinement.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data and suppliers of [F1]–[F3]; work first over the universal

domain $\mathbb Z[z,z^{-1}]$, where all coefficient statements are polynomial

identities, and specialize at the end.

1.1 The row-double-coset identity and membership. For a semistandard tableau $S$ of shape $\lambda$ and type $\rho$ and a standard $t$ of shape $\lambda$, every row-standard refinement $s$ of the column-strict tableau $S$ is standard, and $\sum_sT_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda$ is the sum of $T_w$ over the double coset $S_\rho d(s_0)^{-1}S_\lambda$, each $w$ occurring exactly once; its left $S_\rho$-coset expansion writes it as $x_\rho h_0$, and appending $T_{d(t)}$ gives $m_{(S,t)}=x_\rho h$ for some $h\in H_n$. Hence each $m_{(S,t)}$ lies in $x_\rho H_n$, and no row-intersection quantum factorial is introduced. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Independence and the Garnir coefficient rules. The sums $m_{(S,t)}$ are $R$-independent because their Murphy fibres (the index sets $\{s:\rho(s)=S\}$) are disjoint and every coefficient in the expansion of $m_{(S,t)}$ in the $m_{st}$ basis is $1$; they therefore have disjoint unit pivots. For the coefficient rules, consider a violation at adjacent rows $i,i+1$ and column $j$ and the composition $\nu=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{i-1},j-1,\lambda_i+1,\lambda_{i+1}-j,\lambda_{i+2},\dots)$; the two length-additive coset sums of $S_\nu S_\lambda$ give $\sum_{w\in S_\nu\cap D_\lambda}x_\lambda T_w =\sum_{v\in S_\lambda\cap D_\nu}T_v^*x_\nu,$ whose distinguished Garnir term occurs with coefficient $1$. Every other term in the original shape has strictly more dominant row tableaux, the reordered $\nu$ has strictly higher lexicographic shape, and the ordinary Murphy dominance refinement places these shape errors in higher-cell ideals; a nonstandard tableau factors as that Garnir tableau followed by an additive-length word (removing inversions while keeping the column violation), and Bruhat subword support preserves the strict tableau-prefix inequality. In the isolated relation for consecutive $a,a+1$ in one column, sorting the Garnir belt has a unique standard term whose single adjacent swap produces the distinguished Garnir term, with coefficient $-1$, and every other same-shape term is strictly more dominant. This yields the displayed congruence of the Statement, and the right analogue follows by the cellular involutions $*$. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 The row eigenspace test. For a fixed $a$ the left $z$-eigenspace of $T_a$ in $H_n$ is $(1+T_a)H_n$: in the $T_w$ basis pair $w$ with $s_aw$ of larger length, and coefficient comparison in $T_ah=zh$ gives equality of the two coefficients, whose sum is $(1+T_a)T_w$. This argument uses only that $z$ is a unit. Over the universal domain, no element of this space has a nonzero Murphy coefficient at a tableau with $a,a+1$ in one column: choose a least shape and then a least left tableau in a dominance-compatible support order; higher-cell terms cannot contribute to its shape, and a column correction from another tableau can contribute only from a strictly less dominant left tableau, absent by minimality. If $a,a+1$ are in a column, its coefficient in $T_ah$ is the negative of its coefficient in $h$ by step 1.2, contradicting the eigenvalue equation since $z+1\ne0$ in the domain; if they share a row, the basis element is already a $z$-eigenvector and is subtracted; if their swap is standard, the exact two-tableau rules make the two coefficients equal and their sum is a $z$-eigenvector, which is subtracted. Each subtraction stays in the row ideal and removes the chosen support term without creating new ones, so induction on the finite support proves the column exclusion; specializing the resulting coordinate-zero identities gives it over every base ring, with no division by $z+1$ at a singular parameter. [F1, algebra]

3.1 The basis theorem. Let $h\in x_\rho H_n$. It is a $z$-eigenvector for every generator inside every $\rho$-row interval, so step 2.1 excludes any supported tableau with a consecutive pair inside one column; for an adjacent standard swap, comparison of the exact two-tableau equations makes the two coefficients equal (no column-state correction can interfere, since every such state has coefficient $0$). The standard refinements of a fixed row-label tableau are the linear extensions of the finite node posets of its repeated-label classes, and any two are connected by swaps of adjacent incomparable elements; finite induction on the inversion distance shows that if a repeated label occupies one column, a consecutive vertical cover realises an excluded state and forces the whole fibre coefficient to be $0$, while otherwise the row-label tableau is column-strict and every fibre coefficient equals one common value. Hence $h$ has zero coefficients off semistandard fibres and constant coefficients on each semistandard fibre, i.e. $h$ lies in the span of the $m_{(S,t)}$; with step 1.2 this proves that the $m_{(S,t)}$ form an $R$-basis of $x_\rho H_n$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The two filtrations, keeping the ordinary dictionary explicit. The higher-shape Murphy-cell filtration obtained from [F1] has one quotient $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ for every semistandard tableau $S$ of shape $\lambda$ and type $\rho$: its second-index action is the fixed-first-index Murphy cell action. These quotients are free over $R$, so every short exact sequence of this filtration splits as a sequence of $R$-modules. Star duality is therefore exact on this filtration. On the distinguished coset basis $b_d=x_\rho T_d$ of $x_\rho H_n$, define $\beta(b_d,b_c)=\delta_{dc}z^{\ell(d)}$. The row-permutation generator cases prove contravariance: a same-row generator acts by $z$; a length-increasing adjacent coset pair acts by $b_dT_i=b_c$, $b_cT_i=z b_d+(z-1)b_c$, with $\ell(c)=\ell(d)+1$, and the diagonal weights give $\beta(b_dT_i,b_c)=z^{\ell(c)}=z\beta(b_d,b_d)$. All other entries are zero or the corresponding diagonal equality. Thus $\beta$ gives an $H_n$-isomorphism $x_\rho H_n\cong(x_\rho H_n)^\circ$, since every diagonal $z^{\ell(d)}$ is a unit. The independently proved same-shape bridge gives $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)^\circ\cong P(\lambda)$, the ordinary Dipper–James Specht module, by finite-free biduality. Dualize the split Murphy filtration and transport it through this permutation self-duality. The resulting reversed filtration is an ordinary Specht filtration with exactly the same multiplicities. The original Murphy filtration is not called the ordinary one. This preserves the full every-ring/unit-parameter existence Statement without generic semisimplicity or form nondegeneracy on a Specht module. [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The generic multiplicity interpretation. Over the generic field the finite Hecke algebra is split semisimple: by [F2] every simple is a nonzero cellular head, a simple factor of an ordinary cell module has a word character from that module and from the head's own cell shape, and disjoint word sets force the shapes to agree; existence of a factor forces its own head to be nonzero, diagonal multiplicity $1$ forces the cell module to be simple, and the sum of squared dimensions equals the Hecke rank, so the algebra and each parabolic are split semisimple. Consequently the filtration multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$ equals the multiplicity of the trivial character of the $\rho$-row parabolic in $S^\lambda$, by induction/restriction adjunction in the semisimple category. [F2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 prove the semistandard Murphy basis of $x_\rho H_n$, step 1.2 gives the explicit Garnir and same-column generator rules with their termination, step 4.1 gives the Specht filtration with multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$, and step 5.1 gives the generic parabolic-multiplicity interpretation. Everything is proved universally over $\mathbb Z[z,z^{-1}]$ and specializes; the row-double-coset membership uses each coset word once and introduces no quantum-factorial division. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke algebras of level one are finite Hecke algebras
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$ be a level-one fundamental weight and keep the
conventions of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]. Then the
assignments $T_r\mapsto T_r$ ($1\le r<d$) in the nondegenerate case and
$s_r\mapsto s_r$ in the degenerate case extend to $F$-algebra isomorphisms
$$H_{F,q}(S_d)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_d,\qquad FS_d\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_d$$
respectively ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The level-one quotient $H^\Lambda_d$ and the finite generators

$T_r$ (respectively $s_r$).

1.1 Surjectivity of the natural map. By [F1] the first polynomial generator is the scalar $q^j$ (respectively $j$), and the recursion expressing every $X_{r+1}$ (respectively $x_{r+1}$) in $X_r$ and $T_r$ (respectively $s_r$) shows that the algebra generated by the finite generators and $X_1$ is already generated by the finite generators alone. Hence the assignment of the Statement is a surjective algebra homomorphism. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The inverse in the nondegenerate branch. Let $L_r$ be the additive Jucys–Murphy element and put $M_r:=1+(q-1)L_r=q^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1^{\,2}\cdots T_{r-1},$ a product of units, so every $M_r$ is invertible; the $M_r$ commute because the $L_r$ do, and $T_rM_rT_r=qM_{r+1}$ while $T_rM_t=M_tT_r$ for $t\notin\{r,r+1\}$ follow from [F2] by separating the term $a=r$ in $L_{r+1}$ and using the finite braid relation on the three affected transpositions. Setting $X_r:=q^jM_r$ therefore produces commuting units with $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, distant mixed commutation, the finite Hecke relations and $X_1=q^j$. These elements satisfy the complete affine presentation, so the assignment defines a homomorphism $H^\Lambda_d\to H_{F,q}(S_d)$ fixing the $T_r$. [F1, F2, construct]

1.3 The inverse in the degenerate branch. Put $x_r:=j+L_r$ with $L_r=\sum_{a<r}(a\ r)\in FS_d$. Direct transposition multiplication gives $s_rL_{r+1}s_r=L_r+s_r$, hence $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$, and the $x_r$ commute and commute with distant generators by [F2]; at $r=1$ this gives $x_1=j$. These elements satisfy the degenerate affine relations, so the assignment defines a homomorphism $H^\Lambda_d\to FS_d$ fixing the $s_r$. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Mutual inverses. The two constructions of steps 1.2 and 1.3 fix every finite generator, and the composites with the surjection of step 1.1 fix every presentation generator: the finite generators by construction, and the polynomial generators because both sides satisfy the same recursion from $X_1=q^j$ (respectively $x_1=j$) and the mixed relations. Hence both composites are the identity on a generating set, so the maps are mutually inverse isomorphisms; rank zero gives $F$ on both sides. This removes any late-basis or dimension dependency and introduces no BK or primitive-block input. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

items.title: Affine and cyclotomic type-A Hecke algebras
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$s_r^2=1,\qquad s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1},\qquad s_rs_t=s_ts_r\quad(|r-t|>1);$$
its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by
[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions
$r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one
$\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke
algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).
Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of
unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$)
are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded as a deferred boundary in
the batch notes. These presentations and the charged quotients are the ones of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no
embedding of the label set $I$ into $F$ is claimed in the nondegenerate branch,
and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The pure presentations and charged quotients are [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]. The required field-independent DG ordered basis is the declared local rational-operator/Bruhat-leading proof, not an unconsumed batch17 realization. The level-one fact is proved independently by the explicit JM inverse in the declared proposition. Integer I labels produce distinct spectral values q_H^i in NG and i·1_F in DG; no impossible NG embedding of I into F is used. The original finite-e scope and source normalization are retained.

items.title: The type-A cyclotomic specialization of the QG-KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $F,q,e,I,\Lambda,\lambda_i$ be as in
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]],
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). On the cyclic affine type-A Cartan
datum take the normalized symmetrizers $d_i=1$ and define the **type-A KLR
datum** $Q^{\mathrm A}$ by
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{ii}=0,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1\quad\text{if }a_{ij}=0,$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v\qquad(e\ge3),$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{01}(u,v)=Q^{\mathrm A}_{10}(u,v)=-(u-v)^2\qquad(e=2).$$
Write $R_\alpha$ for the resulting generalized KLR algebra over $F$
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]) and $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ for
the standard cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] (monic first-strand
relations $x_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(\nu)=0$).

**The specialization dictionary.** Put $y_r:=x_r$ and $\psi_r:=-\tau_r$. With
these normalizations, the relations (1.6)–(1.15) of the source hold in
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and conversely the quotient presented by those relations
is the same algebra; in other words $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the sign-modified
cyclotomic Khovanov–Lauda algebra of the source for the cyclic quiver of
quantum characteristic $e$. The verification of the dictionary is elementary
and is recorded here so that no hidden convention is imported:

1. **(Q1)–(Q4).** Non-adjacent pairs have $a_{ij}=0$ and
   $Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1$, homogeneous of degree $0$. For an adjacent pair
   $(i,i+1)$ with $e\ge3$ one has $b_{ij}=a_{ij}=-1$, and $v-u$ is homogeneous
   of degree $2=-2b_{ij}$ with nonzero extremal coefficients of
   $u^{-a_{ij}}=u$ and $v^{-a_{ji}}=v$; the opposite orientation is the
   transpose, so (Q2) is built into the two formulae. For $e=2$ the pair
   $\{0,1\}$ has $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $b_{01}=-2$, and $-(u-v)^2$ is
   symmetric, homogeneous of degree $4=-2b_{01}$, with top coefficient $-1\ne0$.
2. **Dot sliding.** Relation (1.8) comes from $\tau_re(i)=e(s_ri)\tau_r$;
   relations (1.12)–(1.13) reduce to the dot-sliding constants
   $\tau_ax_a-x_{a+1}\tau_a=e(\nu)$ and
   $\tau_ax_{a+1}-x_a\tau_a=-e(\nu)$ on equal colours, whose sign changes to
   the source's constants $+1$ under $\psi=-\tau$.
3. **Quadratic and braid relations.** Relation (1.14): equal colours give
   $\tau^2=Q_{ii}=0$; non-adjacent colours give $\tau^2=1=e(i)$; a forward
   arrow gives $\tau^2=v-u$, evaluated at $(y_r,y_{r+1})$ as
   $y_{r+1}-y_r$; a backward arrow gives $y_r-y_{r+1}$; the $e=2$ double edge
   gives $(y_{r+1}-y_r)(y_r-y_{r+1})$. Relation (1.15): the divided-difference
   numerator
   $\bigl[Q^{\mathrm A}(x_a,x_{a+1})-Q^{\mathrm A}(x_{a+2},x_{a+1})\bigr]/(x_{a+2}-x_a)$
   equals $\pm1$ in the two single-edge cases with $i_{r+2}=i_r$, equals
   $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ in the $e=2$ double-edge case, and vanishes
   otherwise; the global sign $\psi=-\tau$ matches the source's three cases.
   The product order is explicit: the source difference is
   $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_r-\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}$, which under
   $\psi=-\tau$ equals the native reversed-word difference
   $\tau_{r+1}\tau_r\tau_{r+1}-\tau_r\tau_{r+1}\tau_r$; for
   $Q=-(u-v)^2$ the displayed quotient is $u+w-2v$. Thus no braid-order sign
   is suppressed, also in characteristic two.

Degrees of products are read on the successive permuted colour pairs as in
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. This definition introduces
no new basis, trace or primitive-block assertion, and uses no choice
principle.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke intertwiners and local power series
items.statement:
Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector (possibly zero) as in
[[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]], with the residue
tuples $i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ contained in a fixed index set $I_\alpha$.

1. Set $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ in the degenerate case and
   $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ in the nondegenerate case
   ($1\le r\le d$). Then $y_1,\dots,y_d$ are commuting nilpotent elements of
   $H^\Lambda_\alpha$; consequently every rational expression displayed below,
   expanded as a power series in the nilpotent $y$'s, is a finite and
   well-defined element of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.
2. The power series
   $$p_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1}\end{cases}$$
   (degenerate case), respectively
   $$P_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (1-q)\bigl(1-y_r(i)y_{r+1}(i)^{-1}\bigr)^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1},\end{cases} \qquad y_r(i):=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$$
   (nondegenerate case), satisfy (3.23)–(3.25) respectively (4.24)–(4.26),
   (4.28)–(4.30) and (4.32); and the intertwining elements
   $$\varphi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(s_r+p_r(i)\bigr)e(i),\qquad \Phi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(T_r+P_r(i)\bigr)e(i)$$
   satisfy all identities (3.14)–(3.20) of the source's Lemma 3.1,
   respectively (4.14)–(4.20) of its Lemma 4.1.
3. There exist invertible power series $q_r(i)\in F[\![y_r,y_{r+1}]\!]$
   (respectively $Q_r(i)$) satisfying (3.27)–(3.29), respectively
   (4.33)–(4.35); the explicit candidates (3.30) respectively (4.36) do, and
   for them the identity (3.43) respectively (4.44) holds.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data of the Statement and the facts above.

1.1 Finite evaluation. On each projector $e(i)$ the dots are commuting nilpotents by [F1]. If $y_r^{n_r}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than $\sum_r(n_r-1)$ vanishes. Thus formal series have finite evaluation, and $c+f$ with $c\ne0$ and $f$ of positive degree has inverse $c^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-f/c)^k$. Unequal-colour spectral differences have nonzero scalar constant; equal-colour dot differences will only be used as formal divided differences, never inverted in the cyclotomic algebra. [F1, algebra]

1.2 A faithful formal calculation convention. Temporarily take independent dots $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ and a separate copy of their fraction field for each colour word. Let $S_r$ swap both positions and their dots; write multiplication on the right of $S_r$. For spectral variables $A,B$, put $\widehat p=(A-B)^{-1}$ in DG and $\widehat P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, even on equal colours. The affine Hecke operator is $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ in DG and $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ in NG. For precision the formal calculation algebra has coefficients $\bigoplus_i F[\![u_1,\ldots,u_d]\!]e(i)$ and the affine generators, with spectral word-sliding: an unequal-colour intertwiner moves $e(i)$ to $e(s_ri)$ and permutes coefficients, while on equal colours the affine mixed relation gives its divided-difference correction. These relations follow in a sector by the CRT projectors and the mixed presentation: multiply the unequal spectral difference by the intertwiner and use its unit inverse; on equal colours use $H+1$. This calculation is faithful before any cyclotomic quotient: move coefficients right by these mixed and word-sliding relations and reduce crossing words by the Coxeter relations to span the finitely many $H_we(i)$; in their crossed-product expansions the coefficient at a reduced permutation $w$ is a product of nonzero rational functions and every proper subword has smaller length. A maximal-length coefficient therefore proves independence, also for formal series coefficients after clearing their finitely many difference denominators. Consequently an identity between regular formal expressions can be checked in this rational model and then evaluated at nilpotent dots. This is a calculation in the affine presentation, not an assumption that its cyclotomic quotient acts faithfully. [F2, algebra]

2.1 Explicit normalization. Write $u=y_r,v=y_{r+1}$, $p=(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)^{-1}$ on unequal DG colours, and $A=q^{i_r}(1-u),B=q^{i_{r+1}}(1-v)$ on NG colours. In the order equal, unrelated, forward arrow, backward arrow, double edge, choose $q_r(i)$ to be $1+v-u$, $1-p$, $(1-p^2)/(v-u)$, $1$, $(1-p)/(v-u)$, respectively, and choose $Q_r(i)$ to be $1-q+qv-u$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)^2$, $q^{i_r}$, $q^{i_r}/(A-B)$, respectively. These are the actual five branches, including $e=2$. For DG forward colours $i_r-i_{r+1}=-1$, so $1-p^2=(v-u)(2-u+v)/(1-u+v)^2$; on the double edge the field has characteristic two and $1-p=(v-u)/(1+u-v)$. Thus the forward quotient has constant $2\ne0$ unless the pair is a double edge, which uses the separate constant $1$ branch. Unrelated pairs have $i_r-i_{r+1}\ne0,\pm1$, so $1-p$ has nonzero constant. In NG the unequal $A-B$ is a unit; $A-qB$ has nonzero constant except for a backward arrow, whose coefficient is prescribed separately. Hence all five coefficients are units; the equal coefficient has constant $1$ in DG and $1-q\ne0$ in NG. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The full affine coefficient check. In left-coefficient notation $H_{AB}=a_{AB}S+b_{AB}$, use $(h,t)=(1,0)$ in DG and $(q,q-1)$ in NG, where $b_{AB}=-(A-B)^{-1}$ or $(1-q)B/(A-B)$, respectively, and $a_{AB}=h-b_{AB}$. Direct common-denominator multiplication gives $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$. The mixed relations follow by multiplying $A,B$ on either side; the first two identities give $H^2=tH+h$. For three positions, expansion of either braid word has coefficients, in the order $1,S_1,S_2,S_1S_2,S_2S_1,S_1S_2S_1$, equal to $b_{AC}(h+b_{AB}b_{BC})$, $a_{AB}b_{BC}b_{AC}$, $a_{BC}b_{AB}b_{AC}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}b_{BC}$, $a_{BC}a_{AC}b_{AB}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}a_{BC}$. For example the first expansion's constant is $b_{AB}^2b_{BC}+a_{AB}a_{BA}b_{AC}$, which reduces to the displayed constant using the three scalar identities. The $S_1$ coefficient reduces from $a_{AB}(b_{AC}b_{BA}+b_{AB}b_{BC})$ in the same way. Thus this six-coefficient check establishes braid for all spectral triples, including any coincidence of colour labels; spectral variables remain independent at this stage. Disjoint positions commute. [step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Pair products and interchange. Denote the chosen normalizer by $N_{ij}(u,v)$, the piecewise scalar by $p$ in DG or $P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, and put $K_{ij}(u,v)=1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$ in the four unequal-colour cases. Substitution gives $p_{ij}+p_{ji}(v,u)=0$ in DG and $P_{ij}+P_{ji}(v,u)=1-q$ in NG. Also $N_{ij}(u,v)N_{ji}(v,u)K_{ij}(u,v)=1-p_{ij}^2$ in DG and $(1-P_{ij})(q+P_{ij})$ in NG. For the latter equality, its right side is $(B-qA)(A-qB)/((B-A)(A-B))$; forward and backward pairs use $B-qA=q^{i_{r+1}}(u-v)$ and $A-qB=q^{i_r}(v-u)$, respectively, and a double edge uses both. These substitutions prove each branch of the pair-product identities without division by a nonunit. Each coefficient depends only on its ordered two colours and their two dots. Therefore swapping a third position gives the same coefficient of the same ordered pair, proving the three-position interchange identities for $p,P,N$. In particular no square root is chosen. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The intertwiners. On unequal colours $\varphi=S(1-p)$ and $\Phi=S(1-P)$, since the scalar term cancels. Hence they permute the word and the two spectral variables, their squares are the pair products in step 3.1, and they commute at distant positions. On equal colours they are $H+1$; their squares are $2\varphi$ and $(1+q)\Phi$. The equal-colour mixed correction is $1+B-A$ in DG and $qB-A$ in NG, obtained by multiplying the operator $H+1$ by $B$ and subtracting $A(H+1)$. The braid defect is zero unless the outer colours coincide. For all equal colours, expanding $(H_1+1)(H_2+1)(H_1+1)$ minus its reversed word gives $h(\varphi_1-\varphi_2)$ in DG and $q(\Phi_1-\Phi_2)$ in NG (here $h=1$ in DG). For outer equal, middle unequal, write $C_{AB}=1-\widehat p_{AB}$ or $1-\widehat P_{AB}$, and $F_{AB}=C_{AB}C_{BA}$. The middle equal-colour intertwiner contributes either its permutation term or its scalar term $C_{AC}$. The former gives equal longest-permutation coefficients in the two words; the latter gives identity coefficients $F_{AB}C_{AC}$ and $F_{BC}C_{AC}$. Their difference is therefore $C_{AC}(F_{AB}-F_{BC})$. In DG put $p_1=1/(A-B),p_2=1/(B-C)$ and use $p_1+p_2=(A-C)p_1p_2$; then this difference is $(p_1-p_2)(p_1p_2-p_1-p_2)$. In NG, substituting $C_{AC}=(A-qC)/(A-C)$ and $F_{AB}=(A-qB)(B-qA)/(-(A-B)^2)$ cancels the factor $A-C$ and gives $(1-q)^2(AC-B^2)(AB-qBC)/((A-B)^2(B-C)^2)$. Adjacent-equal and distinct-colour patterns have no remaining identity term; their permutation coefficients cancel by the scalar identities of step 2.2. These are precisely the intertwiner identities named in the Statement. [step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 A local crossing calculation that will also serve both relation maps. Put $D_r f=(S_rf-f)/(u_r-u_{r+1})$; every inverse dot difference in an operator formula acts by multiplication on the left unless explicitly included in a right coefficient. On equal colours, $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$, since $1-\widehat p=-N/(u-v)$ in DG and $1-\widehat P=-N/(u-v)$ in NG; thus $(H+1)N^{-1}=D$. On unequal colours set $c_{ij}(u,v)=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$, so the normalized crossing is $S_rc_{ij}$ and $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$ by step 3.1. For a formal coefficient $f$, direct subtraction gives $Df=(Sf)D+(Sf-f)/(u-v)$ and $D^2=0$; unequal crossings simply permute coefficients. These formulas prove the dot-sliding and quadratic relations and the compatibility $\psi_r^2N_r(i)S_rN_r(s_ri)=1-p_r(i)^2$ or $(1-P_r(i))(q+P_r(i))$ on unequal colours; on equal colours both sides of the original compatibility identity are zero. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Every braid colour pattern. Write $u,v,w$ for the three dots, $W=S_1S_2S_1$, and $c=c_{ik}$. If all colours are distinct, both crossing braid words have right coefficient $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$ at $W$. For $(i,i,k)$ both are $(W-S_1S_2)c(u,w)c(v,w)/(v-w)$; the coefficient product is symmetric in $u,v$, so moving it through $D_1$ adds no divided-difference correction. For $(i,k,k)$ both are $(W-S_2S_1)c(u,v)c(u,w)/(u-v)$, by the same calculation with the product symmetric in $v,w$. In these two formulas the denominator multiplies on the left and the coefficient product multiplies on the right. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest-permutation terms cancel by the ordered-pair interchange of step 3.1; the remaining identity coefficients in $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1$ and $\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$ are $-K_{ij}(u,v)/(u-w)$ and $-K_{ij}(w,v)/(u-w)$. Thus their difference is $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$, equal to $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$ for unrelated, forward, backward, double-edge pairs. Finally all equal colours give $D_1D_2D_1=D_2D_1D_2=-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. Each displayed quotient is a formal divided difference; the resulting braid correction is polynomial, including characteristic two. This proves all five cases locally. [step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Regular identities and conclusion. The rational calculations above express every intertwiner, normalization, dot-sliding, quadratic and braid identity as an identity of regular formal expressions in the affine generators. Faithfulness in step 1.2 licenses clearing the temporary differences, and step 1.1 licenses finite evaluation in the sector. The candidate normalizers and their products give all stated identities, retaining $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}y_r(i)$ in NG. Therefore all three assertions of the Statement hold over the original field, with no algebraic closure or choice principle. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: The cyclotomic KLR block satisfies the Hecke relations
items.statement:
In the specialized cyclotomic KLR content algebra $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ define
$$x_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(y_r+i_r)e(i),\qquad s_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\bigl(\psi_rq_r(i)-p_r(i)\bigr)e(i)$$
in the degenerate case and
$$X_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)\bigr)e(i)$$
in the nondegenerate case, where $p,P,q,Q$ are the power series of
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-intertwiners-and-local-power-series]] evaluated in
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$ using the nilpotence of the $y$'s. Then these elements
satisfy the defining relations (3.2)–(3.5), respectively (4.2)–(4.5), of the
affine Hecke algebra and the cyclotomic relation
$\prod_i(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$, respectively
$\prod_i(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}=0$; hence they define a unique $F$-algebra
homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_d\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. Moreover $\sigma$
kills $e_\beta$ and every corner component $e_\beta H^\Lambda_de_\gamma$ with
$(\beta,\gamma)\ne(\alpha,\alpha)$, and restricts to a unital homomorphism
$\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\sigma(e(i))=e(i)$
for $i\in I_\alpha$ and $\sigma(e(i))=0$ otherwise.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The elements of the Statement and the relations of [F1]–[F2].

1.1 A faithful KLR calculation, before quotient. Use independent dots and the rational operators of the normalization supplier’s local crossing and braid calculations: equal crossings act by $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$ and unequal crossings by $Sc_{ij}$, where $c_{ij}=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ in DG or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$ in NG. The pair product is exactly $K_{ij}$ and the five braid computations give corrections $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$, with the specified braid order. Thus these operators satisfy the affine sign-modified KLR presentation. This representation is faithful for formal dot coefficients: moving dots right by the proved sliding rule, use quadratic relations to remove repeated simple reflections and braid relations to reduce each crossing word to a chosen reduced word plus shorter words. This terminates by length (and the finite Coxeter reduction at each fixed length), giving a spanning family $\psi_we(i)$. Its leading permutation coefficient is a product of nonzero $c_{ij}$ and of $1/(u-v)$ for equal pairs; proper subwords have smaller permutation length. Maximal-length comparison in the matrix crossed product therefore proves independence of the formal coefficients. Clearing finitely many temporary dot differences is legitimate in this faithful affine calculation. It does not assert faithfulness after taking the cyclotomic quotient. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The mixed and quadratic computations. In the representation of step 1.1, the displayed inverse Hecke element $\psi N-p$ (DG) or $\psi N-P$ (NG) is literally $S(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ or $S(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ on every word. On unequal colours this follows by cancellation of the right coefficient $N$; on equal colours $\psi=D$ and $D N-1=H$ by the equality $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$. The supplier’s full affine coefficient check gives the mixed relation $Hx_{r+1}-x_rH=1$ in DG, and $HX_rH=qX_{r+1}$ in NG, together with $H^2=1$ or $H^2=(q-1)H+q$. Alternatively the DG mixed constant on an unequal word is $(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)p=1$, and on an equal word it is $(u-v)+N=1$; in NG the same spectral substitution gives the stated mixed identity. Commuting dots, distant mixed relations and distant crossings follow because the operators involve disjoint pairs. By step 1.1 these are regular affine-KLR identities and hence evaluate in the nilpotent-dot quotient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 All five Hecke braid patterns. For a triple with distinct colours, adjacent repeated colours $(i,i,k)$ or $(i,k,k)$, outer repeated colours $(i,j,i)$, or all equal colours, the inverse elements of step 2.1 have precisely the same rational Hecke operator $H$ on each successive word. Their two braid products therefore have the six coefficients listed in the supplier’s full affine coefficient check; this table applies to each of the five patterns because spectral variables, rather than colour constants, are used in its denominators. The required scalar reductions are $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$, with $(h,t)=(1,0)$ or $(q,q-1)$. In the outer-repeated pattern the KLR braid correction $u+w-2v$ on a double edge was already included in the faithful model of step 1.1, so it is not suppressed by this table. In the equal pattern $D$ accounts for all divided-difference terms. Equality of the six explicit coefficients, followed by faithfulness, proves Hecke braid inside the formal KLR algebra; its regular expressions descend to the cyclotomic quotient. This proves the missing four cases and the all-equal case without assuming any Hecke intertwiner relation in that algebra. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The cyclotomic relation and the homomorphism. The cyclotomic relation $\prod_i(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$ (respectively $\prod_i(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}=0$) holds because $y_1^{(\Lambda,\alpha_{i_1})}e(i)=0$ is the cyclotomic KLR relation and $x_1=\sum_i(y_1+i_1)e(i)$ (respectively $X_1=\sum_iq^{i_1}(1-y_1)e(i)$) is a shift of the dot. Hence all defining relations of the affine cyclotomic quotient are satisfied, and the universal property of the presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_d\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ carrying the generators to the displayed elements. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 Identification of $\sigma(e(i))$. By [F2] the algebra $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite-dimensional, so it becomes a finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_d$-module through $\sigma$. The simultaneous generalized weight space for $\sigma(x_r)e(i)=(y_r+i_r)e(i)$ in DG, or $\sigma(X_r)e(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i)$ in NG, on $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is exactly $e(i)R^\Lambda_\alpha$ when $i\in I_\alpha$ and is $0$ otherwise, by the nilpotence of the dots and the weight relation. Hence $\sigma(e(i))$, being the projector onto that generalized weight space for the commuting operators $\sigma(x_1),\dots,\sigma(x_d)$ in DG, or $\sigma(X_1),\dots,\sigma(X_d)$ in NG, equals $e(i)$ for $i\in I_\alpha$ and vanishes otherwise. [F2, step 4.1]

6.1 Factorization through the sector. Since $e_\alpha$ is central and $\sum_\beta e_\beta=1$ in $H^\Lambda_d$ ([[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]]), and since $\sigma$ annihilates all idempotents $e(i)$ with $i\notin I_\alpha$ by step 5.1, the element $\sigma(1-e_\alpha)=0$. Therefore $\sigma$ kills $e_\beta$ for $\beta\ne\alpha$ and every corner $e_\beta H^\Lambda_de_\gamma$ with $(\beta,\gamma)\ne(\alpha,\alpha)$, and it factors through the central summand $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_de_\alpha$ as a unital homomorphism. [step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 produce the homomorphism $\sigma$ from the verified affine and cyclotomic relations; steps 5.1 and 6.1 identify its action on the content idempotents and show that it kills all other sector corners, restricting to a unital homomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. No choice principle is used. [step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: Hecke intertwiners produce the local KLR generators
items.statement:
Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector, possibly zero, as in
[[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]], and let $y_r$ be the
elements of [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-intertwiners-and-local-power-series]]. Put
$$\psi_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\varphi_rq_r(i)^{-1}e(i)\quad\text{(degenerate case)}, \qquad \psi_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}e(i)\quad\text{(nondegenerate case)}.$$
Then the elements $\{e(i):i\in I_\alpha\}\cup\{y_1,\dots,y_d\}\cup
\{\psi_1,\dots,\psi_{d-1}\}$ of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ satisfy the relations
(1.6)–(1.15) of the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR presentation of
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. Consequently
there is a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism
$\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $e(i)\mapsto e(i)$,
$y_r\mapsto y_r$ and $\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The displayed elements $\psi_r$ and the identities of [F1]–[F2].

1.1 The cyclotomic and dot-sliding relations. The first KLR relation follows from the cyclotomic relation [F2] and the invertibility of $(x_1-i_1)$ respectively $(1-q^{-i_1}X_1)$ off the summand $e(i)$: on $e(i)$ the dot $y_1$ is nilpotent and $x_1=y_1+i_1$ respectively $X_1=q^{i_1}(1-y_1)$, so $y_1^{(\Lambda,\alpha_{i_1})}e(i)=0$ accompanies the cyclotomic relation. The dot and idempotent relations are immediate from the definitions of the idempotents $e(i)$ and the dots $y_r$, and the dot-sliding relations follow from the dot-sliding intertwiner identities, the definitions of $p_r(i),P_r(i)$ and the equal-colour case of the normalization. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Quadratic and all braid patterns. Work first in the faithful formal affine-Hecke calculation of the normalization supplier, then evaluate its regular identities in the sector. On equal colours the normalized intertwiner is $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$, so $D^2=0$ and $Dv-uD=1=vD-Du$. On unequal colours it is $Sc_{ij}(u,v)$, with $c=(1-p)/N$ in DG or $(1-P)/N$ in NG; its square is $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$, giving respectively $1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$. For the braid, put $W=S_1S_2S_1$ and dots $u,v,w$. Distinct colours give both words $Wc_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$. For $(i,i,k)$ both words are $(W-S_1S_2)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{ik}(v,w)/(v-w)$; for $(i,k,k)$ they are $(W-S_2S_1)c_{ik}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)/(u-v)$, with denominators on the left and coefficient products on the right. The products are symmetric in the two equal-colour variables, so their divided differences vanish. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest terms cancel and the identity coefficients differ by $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$; direct substitution gives $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$. On all equal colours the common value is $-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. These are the supplier's explicit local computations, using only affine-Hecke relations and scalar normalizers, not the opposite relation-map lemma. The double-edge correction and its sign remain valid in characteristic two. Clearing temporary differences in the faithful formal calculation gives regular relations; only those relations, and unit coefficients, are evaluated on nilpotent dots. Hence each of the BK quadratic and braid equations holds in $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The homomorphism. The verified relations are exactly the presentation of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ recalled in [F2] and in [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], so the universal property of that presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ sending the generators to the displayed elements. No choice principle is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 verify all relations of the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR presentation for $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$, and step 2.1 invokes the universal property to produce $\rho$. The zero sector is included: all constructions are supported on the projectors $e(i)$, which may vanish. [step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke central sectors are isomorphic to type-A cyclotomic KLR algebras
items.statement:
Over any field $F$ in the charged finite-$e$ conventions, the explicit maps
$$\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha,\qquad \sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$$
from [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually
inverse, for every content $\alpha$, including zero sectors. Here
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is only the central CRT content sector; no primitivity is
assumed. Thus $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if and only if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$, and
summing over the finite height-$d$ contents gives
$$H^\Lambda_d\cong\bigoplus_\alpha R^\Lambda_\alpha .$$
On idempotents the maps are the literal identity, and the dot image is
$x_r-i_r$ in the degenerate branch and $1-q_H^{-i_r}X_r$ in the nondegenerate
branch. This result precedes the late dimension, basis and primitive-block
theorems, and no algebraic-closure hypothesis is required.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The maps $\rho,\sigma$ of [F1]–[F2] over the actual field $F$.

1.1 The forward composite on dots and crossings. On each KLR word the map $\sigma$ kills all idempotents outside content $\alpha$; in particular, since the inverse polynomial generators of $R$ have exactly the eigenword projectors $e(\nu)$ (the nilpotent dots shift distinct scalar eigenvalues), $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ and $\sigma$ annihilates every other central sector. The composite $\sigma\rho$ fixes $y_r$ by [F2], and on a crossing $\sigma\bigl(\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}e(i)\bigr) =\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)+P_r(i)\bigr)Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)=\psi_re(i),$ using the definitions of the local generating elements in [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]]; the degenerate case is the same computation with $\varphi_r,p_r,q_r$ in place of $\Phi_r,P_r,Q_r$. These are literal ordered expressions, not a commutation of $\psi_r$ with its coefficient. Hence $\sigma\rho$ fixes every presentation generator of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The reverse composite on generators. By [F2] the composite $\rho\sigma$ fixes the idempotents and dots; on a word, $\rho\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)\bigr)e(i) =\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}Q_r(i)e(i)-P_r(i)e(i) =T_re(i)$ in the nondegenerate case, and the same with $s_r$ in the degenerate case. Again the evaluation is a finite expression in the nilpotent variables. For the polynomial generators the computations are $\rho\sigma(x_re_\alpha)=\sum_i((x_r-i_r)+i_r)e(i)=x_re_\alpha$ in DG and $\rho\sigma(X_re_\alpha)=\sum_iq^{i_r}(1-(1-q^{-i_r}X_r))e(i)=X_re_\alpha$ in NG; their inverses are fixed because homomorphisms preserve inverses. Conversely $\sigma\rho(y_re(i))=(\sigma(x_r)-i_r)e(i)=y_re(i)$ in DG and $(1-q^{-i_r}\sigma(X_r))e(i)=y_re(i)$ in NG. Along with the projector identities of [F1], these verify every presentation generator of both algebras, including the correct inverse NG substitution. Hence $\rho\sigma$ fixes every presentation generator of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F2, algebra]

2.1 Mutual inverses and the zero-sector statement. Both composites fix all generators of their source algebras, so $\rho\sigma=\operatorname{id}$ and $\sigma\rho=\operatorname{id}$; in particular the maps are algebra isomorphisms, and on idempotents they are the literal identity. If $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ then the already constructed $\sigma$ would satisfy $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ with $e_\alpha=0$, forcing $1_R=0$; conversely the forward identities force $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$. Zero rings and rank zero are therefore included without any nonzero-block premise. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Conclusion. Summing the isomorphisms over the finite set of height-$d$ contents and using that the $e_\alpha$ are central orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ by [F3] gives $H^\Lambda_d\cong\bigoplus_\alpha R^\Lambda_\alpha$. Neither exact dimension nor primitive terminology has entered the proof; the full colour-case verifications, affine six-coefficient calculation and equal-colour divided-difference computation reside in the normalization supplier and the two preceding local relation lemmas. No choice principle and no algebraic closure are used. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Basis and dimension of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement:
With the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], the images of the ordered
monomials
$$x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w\quad(0\le m_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d)$$
in the degenerate case, respectively
$$X_1^{m_1}\cdots X_d^{m_d}T_w\quad(0\le m_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d)$$
in the nondegenerate case, form an $F$-basis of $H^\Lambda_d$. In particular
$\dim_FH^\Lambda_d=\ell^dd!$ and $H^\Lambda_d$ is finite dimensional. For
$d=0$ the singleton empty word gives $H^\Lambda_0=F$ and dimension one
independently of $\ell$. If $\ell=0$ and $d>0$, the relation $1=0$ gives the
zero algebra and the empty basis; no ambiguous $0^0$ convention is used.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data and suppliers of [F1]–[F3]; first assume $d>0$ and

$\ell>0$.

1.1 Exactly $\ell^dd!$ spanning words. By [F1] the bounded ordered monomials span $H^\Lambda_d$, and the number of tuples $(m_1,\dots,m_d,w)$ with $0\le m_r<\ell$ and $w\in S_d$ is $\ell^dd!$. The spanning lemma is stated before, and independent of, the spectral/projector construction, and never imposes the first polynomial independently on every dot. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The dimension. By the sector isomorphism [F2] the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the direct sum of the finite family of sector algebras $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ (one for each content $\alpha$ of height $d$), and each $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is isomorphic to the corresponding summand $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of the specialized KLR algebra. Summing dimensions, $\dim_FH^\Lambda_d=\sum_{\operatorname{ht}\alpha=d}\dim_FH^\Lambda_\alpha =\sum_{\operatorname{ht}\alpha=d}\dim_FR^\Lambda_\alpha =\dim_FB_d=\ell^dd!,$ the last equality being the total dimension statement of [[lem-cyclic-type-a-cyclotomic-klr-regular-hom-norm-gives-total-dimension]]; grouping the root components $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ by their content $\alpha$ is legitimate because the idempotents of distinct contents are orthogonal. This is an integer identity, not an equality reduced modulo the characteristic. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Basis and boundary cases. A spanning family of $\ell^dd!$ vectors in the $\ell^dd!$-dimensional space $H^\Lambda_d$ is a basis, so the bounded ordered monomials form an $F$-basis and $\dim_FH^\Lambda_d=\ell^dd!$. For $d=0$ the singleton empty word gives $H^\Lambda_0=F$ independently of $\ell$; for $\ell=0$ and $d>0$ the imposed relation is $1=0$, the algebra is zero and the empty family is its basis. No ambiguous $0^0$ convention is used. The late theorem does not feed the CRT or the early BK construction, and no Frobenius theorem or global highest-weight isometry is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: Universal cyclotomic Hecke ordered monomials form a basis
items.statement:
Let $R=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ with $\ell\ge1$,
and let $H_n$ be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] at the
first polynomial $\prod_a(X_1-U_a)$. Then $H_n$ is a free $R$-module with
indexed $R$-basis
$$X^aT_w,\qquad 0\le a_r<\ell,\ w\in S_n .$$
This basis specializes to every commutative $R$-algebra. Rank zero is $R$ with
the singleton empty word. The separate level-zero positive-rank quotient is
zero with the empty family.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The universal presentation, the bounded family $\mathcal B$, and

the suppliers of [F1]–[F3].

1.1 Spanning over $R$. By [F1] the family $\mathcal B$ spans $H_n$ over the universal ring $R$: every element is an $R$-combination of the bounded ordered monomials with $0\le a_r<\ell$ and $w\in S_n$. The calculation uses no field division and therefore holds over $R$; for $n=0$ the singleton empty word gives $H_0=R$, and for $\ell=0$, $n>0$ the quotient is zero with the empty family. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Independence by finite-field specialization. Suppose $\sum_b f_bb=0$ is a nontrivial relation in $H_n$ with $f_b\in R$, not all zero. Fix $b_0$ with $f:=f_{b_0}\ne0$ and multiply the relation by a Laurent monomial so that $f\in\mathbb Z[z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell]$; choose a prime $p$ for which some nonzero integer coefficient of $f$ survives modulo $p$, and view $f$ as a polynomial in $U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ with coefficients in $\mathbb F_p[z]$; let $g(z)\ne0$ be one of those coefficients. By [F3] the number of primitive elements of $\mathbb F_{p^d}^\times$ is $\varphi(p^d-1)$, which is unbounded and satisfies $\varphi(N)\ge\sqrt{N/2}$ (factor $N$ over prime powers: each factor $\varphi(r^a)^2/r^a=r^{a-2}(r-1)^2\ge1$ except $r=2$, $a=1$, where it is $1/2$). Choose $d$ with $\varphi(p^d-1)>\deg g$ and $p^d-1$ larger than every $U$-degree of $f$; then some primitive $z\in\mathbb F_{p^d}^\times$ avoids the roots of $g$. Repeated one-variable root bounds on the nonzero-coordinate grid (each $U_a$ is constrained to be a power $z^{c_a}\ne0$, and the remaining polynomial in the next variable has degree bounded by the $U$-degree of $f$) supply $U_a=z^{c_a}\ne0$ with $f(z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell)\ne0$ in $\mathbb F_{p^d}$. This specialization is exactly an allowed finite cyclic type-A field parameter: $z$ has order $e=p^d-1\ge2$, and the cyclotomic charges $c_a$ lie in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 The specialized basis forces a contradiction. Over the field $\mathbb F_{p^d}$ with the parameter and charges of step 1.2, the early explicit BK maps identify the direct sum of the Hecke central sectors with the standard homogeneous cyclic KLR algebra, whose total dimension is $\ell^nn!$ by [F2]. The bounded spanning of step 1.1 provides exactly $\ell^nn!$ ordered words $X^aT_w$, so over the specialized field the family $\mathcal B$ is a basis; specializing the assumed relation forces $f_b(z,U)=0$ for every $b$, and in particular $f(z,U)=0$, contradicting the choice of $z,U$ in step 1.2. Hence the relation was trivial, the family $\mathcal B$ is $R$-linearly independent, and with step 1.1 it is an $R$-basis of $H_n$. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Base change and boundary cases. Formation of the presented algebra commutes with arbitrary base change: the presentation is a quotient of a free algebra and its specialized ideal is precisely the specialized relation ideal, so the $R$-basis $\mathcal B$ specializes to a basis of $H_n\otimes_RR'$ for every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$ (in particular for the LM deformation DVR with $z=q_Ht$ and $U_a=Q_at^{na}$). No integral freeness was inferred from generic rank, no flatness was assumed, and no Schur or primitive-block classification was used. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke center is the symmetric polynomial image
items.statement:
Let $F$ be any field of characteristic $e>0$ with $e\ge2$, and let
$H_d^\Lambda$ be the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra with the FIRST
relation $f(x_1)=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$,
$\lambda_i\ge0$, $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ge1$
([[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]). Then $Z(H_d^\Lambda)$
is exactly the image of $F[t_1,\dots,t_d]^{S_d}$ under $t_r\mapsto x_r$
([[def-symmetric-polynomial]],
[[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]). The proof is over
the original $F$, for every $d\ge0$ and level $\ell$, and does not divide by
$\ell$ or $d!$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data of [F1]–[F2]; rank zero is $F$ with symmetric image $F$,

so assume $d\ge1$.

1.1 The associated graded. Give $x_i$ degree $1$ and the symmetric group degree $0$. By [F1] the transported relation has leading term $x_i^\ell$ with all other dot terms of total degree below $\ell$, and the bounded reduction sends monomials of dot degree $\le r$ to bounded monomials of dot degree $\le r$; independence of the bounded basis makes these the filtration steps $F_r$. The leading mixed relations give the variable permutation action of $S_d$, and the transported relations give $x_i^\ell=0$ in the associated graded. Hence the natural surjection $F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d \longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}H_d^\Lambda$ is an isomorphism: the bounded monomials of the truncated algebra map degree-by-degree onto the basis of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Symmetric polynomials are central. For $x=x_i$, $y=x_{i+1}$, $s=s_i$ the relations of [F2] give, by induction on products, $sg(x,y)-g(y,x)s=\frac{g(y,x)-g(x,y)}{x-y}$ for every polynomial $g$; the quotient is a polynomial because the numerator vanishes at $x=y$. Applying this to a polynomial symmetric in $x,y$ shows that it commutes with $s$, and a globally symmetric polynomial commutes with every $s_i$ and every $x_j$, hence is central in $H_d^\Lambda$. No division by an integer or by $x-y$ inside the algebra is used. [F2, algebra]

2.1 Cycle coefficients in the graded centralizer. In $B=F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d$, put $h_r(I)=\sum X^b$ over $0\le b_i<\ell$ and $\sum_{i\in I}b_i=(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, and $A^{(r)}=h_r(I)A$ for a cycle $A$ on $I$, $0\le r<\ell$. For a coefficient $gA$ commuting with the $X_i$, the equations are $(X_i-X_{A(i)})g=0$. On one cycle they equate coefficients obtained by transferring one unit between consecutive coordinates, with out-of-range coefficients interpreted as zero. At fixed total degree, transfer units until the first $|I|-1$ coordinates are $\ell-1$. If the total is $(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, every coefficient equals the coefficient at $(\ell-1,\dots,\ell-1,r)$; if the total is smaller, the same transfers reach a zero coordinate followed by a transfer to exponent $-1$, and all coefficients vanish. Thus the solutions on that cycle have basis $h_0(I),\dots,h_{\ell-1}(I)$. For disjoint cycles apply these equations separately to each coefficient in the monomial basis of the complementary variables; this gives exactly the products of disjoint colored cycles as the polynomial centralizer basis. This argument also covers $\ell=1$: the truncated polynomial ring is $F$, and its centralizer is $FS_d$. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Reduced-degree powers. Write $f(t)=t^\ell+c_1t^{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_\ell$. The mixed relations give $x_{i+1}^\ell=s_ix_i^\ell s_i+\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}x_i^t x_{i+1}^{\ell-1-t}s_i$. Starting with $x_1^\ell=-\sum_{a=1}^\ell c_ax_1^{\ell-a}$, induction on $i$ shows that $x_i^\ell$ has filtration degree at most $\ell-1$ and symbol $Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1}$ there, where $Y_i=\sum_{j<i}(j\ i)^{(0)}$. For $k=p\ell+r$, $0\le r<\ell$, it follows that $x_i^k$ has filtration degree at most $p(\ell-1)+r$ and symbol $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^pX_i^r$. This is a reduced degree: the ordinary degree-$k$ symbol may be zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Orbit sums and colored-cycle multiplication. Conjugation permutes the basis of step 2.1, so its fixed vectors have basis the orbit sums $z_\lambda$, indexed by colored cycle types, including trivial color-zero fixed points to fill rank $d$. No averaging is used. If $|I\cap J|=c>0$, direct multiplication gives $h_r(I)h_s(J)=\ell^{c-1}h_{r+s+(c-1)(\ell-1)}(I\cup J)$. For $c=1$, fixing the exponents away from the common variable fixes its exponent uniquely and gives the asserted coefficient one. For $c=2$, the basic repeated-edge computation is $h_0(i,j)^2=\ell X_i^{\ell-1}X_j^{\ell-1}$: only equal complementary exponents survive, with exactly $\ell$ choices. Joining the remaining common variables successively reduces the general case to these two computations. Consequently disjoint colored cycles commute; two cycles meeting at one point multiply to their merged cycle of color $r+s$; when they meet in at least two points the product vanishes unless $r=s=0$, and otherwise is a scalar times disjoint cycles all of color $\ell-1$. Indeed the displayed exponent equals the maximal degree on the union when $c=2$, and exceeds it when $c>2$ and $\ell>1$; when $\ell=1$ every polynomial coefficient is one and the assertion reduces to ordinary cycle multiplication. Iterating gives disjoint-cycle reductions, never increasing the union of supports. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The star-cycle expansion. Let $y_i(p\ell+r)$ be the sum of $(j_1\ \cdots\ j_p\ i)^{(r)}$ over ordered, distinct $j_1,\dots,j_p<i$, and let $y_i(0)=1$. Expanding $Y_i^p$, sequences with distinct leaves give precisely $y_i(p\ell)$: the product of the star transpositions is one cycle, with a unique ordered leaf sequence for each such cycle. Any repeated leaf uses at most $p$ vertices including $i$; at its first repetition the intersecting cycles have at least two common vertices, so step 3.1 turns the result into saturated (color $\ell-1$) disjoint cycles or zero. Further star factors preserve saturation by the one-point rule, or vanish by the multiple-point rule. The term $X_i^{\ell-1}$ is itself a saturated singleton containing $i$; choosing it anywhere in $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^p$ has the same consequence and uses at most $p$ vertices. Thus this power equals $y_i(p\ell)$ plus saturated disjoint-cycle products on at most $p$ vertices, always with $i$ in their support. Multiplication by $X_i^r$ gives exactly $y_i(p\ell+r)$ when $r>0$, because it raises the color of the distinct-leaf cycle to $r$, while every saturated error containing $i$ vanishes. (For $\ell=1$ there is no $r>0$ case.) This proves the complete power-symbol formula, including $p=0$. [step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 Triangular symmetric lifts. Index colored cycle types by partitions $\mu$ obtained by replacing each cycle of length $a$ and color $r$ by $k=(a-1)\ell+r$ and discarding zero parts. These are exactly the partitions satisfying $N(\mu)=\operatorname{length}(\mu)+\sum_j\lfloor\mu_j/\ell\rfloor\le d$; the inverse adds $d-N(\mu)$ trivial fixed points. Put $D(\mu)=\sum_j(\mu_j-\lfloor\mu_j/\ell\rfloor)$ and $p_\mu=\sum_{\nu\sim(\mu,0,\dots,0)}x_1^{\nu_1}\cdots x_d^{\nu_d}$, summing each distinct exponent tuple once. It is central by step 1.2 and lies in filtration degree $D(\mu)$ by step 4.1. Its symbol at that degree is $z_\mu$ plus orbit sums with strictly smaller $N$: each product of the leading star cycles on disjoint supports has the prescribed type, and its coefficient is one, since each cycle's largest vertex uniquely chooses its star hub, its ordered other vertices uniquely choose its star expansion, and the unordered exponent tuple chooses each assignment only once, even for repeated parts. Overlapping supports strictly decrease the number of used vertices, as does every error from step 4.1; disjoint-cycle reduction preserves this bound. The entire symbol is central, so the remainder is a combination of orbit sums by step 3.1, with smaller $N$ and the same homogeneous degree. Hence, ordering the finite colored types by $N$, the symbols of the $p_\mu$ form a unit triangular change of the orbit-sum basis, degree by degree. [step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Filtration descent. If $z\in Z(H_d^\Lambda)$ has filtration degree $D$, its degree-$D$ symbol lies in $Z(B)$. By step 5.1 it is a linear combination of degree-$D$ symbols of central symmetric evaluations $p_\mu$; subtract that same combination in $H_d^\Lambda$ to lower the filtration degree. Repeating terminates because degrees are nonnegative; in degree zero the same triangular basis applies, and the next filtration step is zero. Thus every central element is a symmetric-polynomial evaluation, and step 1.2 proves the reverse inclusion. Rank zero was handled separately. No division by $\ell$, $d!$ or the field characteristic occurs. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: The universal cyclotomic Hecke canonical trace is perfect and symmetric
items.statement:
For the universal cyclotomic presentation of
[[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], extract
the coefficient of the zero-dot identity-permutation PBW word to define the
$R$-linear map $\tau$. Then $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ and the pairing
$(a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)$ is a perfect $R$-bilinear associative pairing. Both
properties hold after every commutative unit-parameter base change, including
the LM deformation DVR. Rank zero is $R$ with $\tau(1)=1_R$. For the separate
level-zero positive-rank zero algebra the zero pairing is perfect; no nonzero
$\tau(1)=1$ assertion is made.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The universal PBW presentation and the data of [F1]–[F3].

1.1 The trace and its dual basis. Define $\tau\colon H_n\to R$ by $\tau(\mathcal B)=1$ at the zero-dot identity word and $0$ at every other PBW basis element, extended $R$-linearly; by [F1] this is well defined over $R$ and after base change. Put $J_1=1$ and $J_i=q_H^{-1}T_{i-1}J_{i-1}T_{i-1}$ in the finite Hecke subalgebra; the $J_i$ are units. Define the second family $\mathcal C=\bigl\{T_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)} X_1^{c_1}\cdots X_n^{c_n}:0\le c_i<\ell,\ v\in S_n\bigr\},\qquad \delta(0)=0,\ \delta(c)=-1\ (c>0).$ The standard anti-involution fixing the presentation generators fixes each $X_i$, so $\mathcal B^*=\{T_vX^c\}$ is a basis; at each fixed profile $c$, multiplying the finite Hecke factor by the unit $J_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)}$ is an invertible $R$-linear change of the finite Hecke basis. Hence $\mathcal C$ is an $R$-basis of $H_n$. [F1, construct]

1.2 Cyclicity for $X_1$ via the tower. At rank one the algebra is commutative, so cyclicity is immediate; for the induction assume $n\ge2$. Identify $H_{n-1}$ with the subalgebra on $X_1,\dots,X_{n-1},T_1,\dots,T_{n-2}$; its bounded words are a subset of $\mathcal B$. Put $v_k=s_{n-1}\cdots s_k$ for $1\le k<n$ and $v_n=1$; the decomposition $w=uv_k$ with $u\in S_{n-1}$ is length additive, so $\{X_n^aT_{v_k}:0\le a<\ell,\ 1\le k\le n\}$ is a left $H_{n-1}$-basis of $H_n$. Define the left-linear projection $E_n\colon H_n\to H_{n-1}$ to be $1$ on $X_n^0T_{v_n}$ and $0$ on the other basis elements, and $\tau_n=\tau_{n-1}\circ E_n$. With $V=T_{n-1}\cdots T_1$ and $U=(T_{n-1}-q_H+1)\cdots(T_1-q_H+1)$, the mixed relation gives $VX_1=X_nU$, and [F2] gives $VX_1^m=X_n^mU+J_m$, where every term of $J_m$ has total dot degree $m$ and $X_n$-degree between $1$ and $m-1$ (the leading branch transfers the full exponent, each correction transfers a strictly smaller positive exponent, and no variable above $n$ occurs). For $m\le\ell$ every lower exponent in $J_m$ is below $\ell$, so $E_n(J_m)=0$; likewise $E_n(X_n^mU)=0$ for $1\le m<\ell$. Multiplying the first-dot relation $f(X_1)=0$ by $V$ gives $0=X_n^\ell U+J_\ell+\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}c_m(X_n^mU+J_m)+c_0V$, and applying $E_n$ yields $E_n(X_n^\ell U)=0$, which completes the missing case $m=\ell$. To verify right $X_1$-linearity, test the displayed left tower basis $X_n^aT_{v_k}$. For $k\ge2$, $T_{v_k}$ and $X_n$ commute with $X_1$; its projection is zero unless $a=0,k=n$, where the equality is immediate. For $k=1$, $VX_1=X_nU$ gives $E_n(X_n^aVX_1)=E_n(X_n^{a+1}U)=0$ for $0\le a<\ell$: bounded positive exponents project to zero, and the endpoint $a+1=\ell$ was just established. Left $H_{n-1}$-linearity then extends the equality to every $h$. Hence $E_n(hX_1)=E_n(h)X_1$ for all $h$, and by left linearity $E_n(X_1h)=X_1E_n(h)$; induction on $n$ gives $\tau_n(X_1h)=\tau_n(hX_1)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 Cyclicity for the finite generators. Let $p=X^a$ be a bounded dot monomial and $w\in S_n$. By [F2], $T_jp=(s_jp)T_j+(1-q_H)X_{j+1}\frac{p-s_jp}{X_j-X_{j+1}};$ for $p=X_j^aX_{j+1}^b$ times the other variables, the correction monomials have the same total dot degree and both displayed exponents at most $\max(a,b)<\ell$ (the exponents run as $(a-1-k,b+1+k)$ or $(a+k,b-k)$), so when the exponent profile is positive every term on either side of $\tau(T_jpT_w)=\tau(pT_wT_j)$ has a positive bounded profile and evaluates to $0$. When $p=1$, the finite Hecke multiplication formula [F1] gives coefficient of $1$ in $T_jT_w$, respectively $T_wT_j$, equal to $q_H$ if $w=s_j$ and $0$ otherwise. This proves $\tau(T_jh)=\tau(hT_j)$ without using the trace one is proving. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Generation and symmetry. The elements $X_1,T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ generate $H_n$ as an $R$-algebra: the constant term $c_0=(-1)^\ell\prod_aQ_a$ is a unit, so $f(X_1)=0$ makes $X_1^{-1}$ a polynomial in $X_1$; each $T_j^{-1}=q_H^{-1}(T_j-q_H+1)$; and $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$, with inverses expressed likewise. Moving the generators of a word one at a time around $\tau$, using steps 1.2 and 1.3, gives $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for every pair of words, hence for all $a,b$ by $R$-bilinearity; the pairing $(a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)$ is associative and symmetric. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 Restricted-profile zero values. For $0\le j\le n$ let $U_j$ be the span of the PBW words whose dot entries above $j$ vanish, all finite permutations included. It is a right finite-Hecke module. Multiplying its dot part by any polynomial in $X_1,\dots,X_j$ stays in $U_j$: transport the first cyclotomic relation successively only through $T_1,\dots,T_{j-1}$, so each resulting relation reduces a power of $X_i$, $i\le j$, using variables of index at most $i$ and finite words of indices below $i$; repeated Bernstein straightening and the bounded reduction of [F1] therefore never introduce a variable above $j$. In particular $U_j$ is the dot algebra on its first $j$ variables times the finite Hecke algebra. For $1\le k<\ell$ and $h\in U_j$, $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=0$, directly from the bounded basis, since the new exponent is positive and bounded. This statement concerns $h\in U_j$, rather than arbitrary $h\in H_n$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Transferred restricted-profile powers. Write $q=q_H$. For $1\le i\le j+1\le n$, $1\le k\le\ell$ and $h\in U_j$ we claim $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=q^{i-j-1}\tau(T_j\cdots T_iX_i^kT_i\cdots T_jh)$, with empty chains when $i=j+1$. The mixed relations give $X_i^k=q^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}^kT_{i-1}+q^{-1}(q-1)\sum_{c=1}^{k-1}X_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}$, by induction on $k$ using that $T_{i-1}$ commutes with $X_{i-1}X_i$. To descend from $i$ to $i-1$, it suffices to show every correction has trace zero. Put $A=T_j\cdots T_i$, $B=T_i\cdots T_j$. For $0<c<k$, the mixed relation and the formula $X_{j+1}=q^{i-j-1}AX_iB$ give the exact identity $AX_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}Bh=q^{j-i+1}AX_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}X_{i-1}h$: substitute $B=q^{j-i+1}X_i^{-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}$ and use $X_iT_{i-1}X_i^{-1}=X_{i-1}^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}$. Expand $X_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}$ in the reversed PBW order $\sum a_{w,b}T_wX^b$ using $T_a^{-1}=q^{-1}(T_a+1-q)$. Bernstein straightening swaps the two exponents or replaces them by intermediate exponents, so every exponent stays nonnegative and at most $\max(c-1,k-c-1)\le k-2$; variables have index at most $j+1$. Cyclicity from step 2.1 makes the trace of each correction a sum of traces of $X_{j+1}^{1+b_{j+1}}(X_1^{b_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j})X_{i-1}hAT_w$. The parenthesized remaining factor lies in $U_j$ by step 2.2, and $1\le1+b_{j+1}\le k-1<\ell$, so each trace is zero. Downward induction proves the claim, including $k=1$, whose correction sum is empty. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 The cyclotomic endpoint. Apply step 3.1 with $i=1$, $k=\ell$. In $\tau(q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1X_1^\ell T_1\cdots T_jh)$ replace $X_1^\ell$ using its first cyclotomic relation. Each positive power $X_1^k$, $k<\ell$, transfers back to $X_{j+1}^k$ by step 3.1 and contributes zero by step 2.2. The constant term contributes $\alpha\tau(J_{j+1}h)$, where $\alpha=-f(0)=(-1)^{\ell+1}Q_1\cdots Q_\ell$ and $J_{j+1}=q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1T_1\cdots T_j$. Thus $\tau(X_{j+1}^\ell h)=\alpha\tau(hJ_{j+1})$ for every $h\in U_j$. For $j=0$ this follows directly from the first polynomial; for $\ell=1$ there are no positive-power intermediate terms. The restriction on $h$ is essential. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The full Gram blocks. Let $\mathcal B_j$ and $\mathcal C_j$ be the parts of the two bases with entries above $j$ zero, and let $G_j=(\tau(bc))$ be their matrix, of size $N_j=\ell^jn!$. For new profiles $b,c$ at position $j+1$, cyclicity and commuting dots rewrite an entry as $\tau(X_{j+1}^{b+c}hJ_{j+1}^{\delta(c)})$, where $h=X_1^{b_1+c_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j+c_j}T_wT_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_j^{\delta(c_j)}\in U_j$ by step 2.2; earlier combined exponents may exceed $\ell-1$, and that same reduction argument is why this remains in $U_j$. If $b=c=0$ the block is $G_j$. If $0<b+c<\ell$ it is zero by step 2.2. If $b+c=\ell$, then $c>0$ and step 4.1 cancels the last $J_{j+1}^{-1}$, giving the block $\alpha G_j$. Order rows by $b=0,1,\dots,\ell-1$ and columns by $c=0,\ell-1,\dots,1$. The row and column at zero have only $G_j$ at their intersection. Among positive rows and columns the blocks above the diagonal have $b+c<\ell$ and vanish, the diagonal has $b+c=\ell$, and blocks below may be arbitrary. Hence $G_{j+1}$ is block lower triangular with diagonal $G_j,\alpha G_j,\dots,\alpha G_j$, so $\det G_{j+1}=\pm\alpha^{(\ell-1)N_j}(\det G_j)^\ell$. At $j=0$, $G_0=(\tau(T_wT_v))$ has entry $q^{\operatorname{length}(w)}\delta_{v,w^{-1}}$ by [F1], and its determinant is a unit. Induction gives a unit determinant for $G_n$; since $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$ are bases, the pairing identifies $H_n$ with its $R$-dual. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Base change and boundary cases. Presentation base change commutes with forming $H_n$, and the universal PBW basis is free, so the trace coefficients and the inverse Gram matrix base-change to any commutative ring in which all parameters remain units; in particular they do so for the LM deformation DVR with $q_Ht$ and $Q_at^{na}$. For $n=0$ use $H_0=R$ with $\tau(1)=1_R$; for $\ell=1$ the family $\mathcal C$ consists of finite $T_v$ and the same proof applies. The separate level-zero positive-rank quotient is $0$, with the zero perfect pairing, and no claim $\tau(1)=1$ is made for it. No generic faithfulness or imported Bremke–Malle trace statement is used. [step 1.1, step 5.1] ∎

references.locator: Cached complete 15-page author preprint; §3, printed pp. 5–9, especially Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8. Local restricted-profile computations below reconstruct the proof; the sign alpha is obtained directly from the cyclotomic polynomial.
