items.title: Cyclotomic Jantzen equivalence is Schur and Hecke block linkage
items.statement:
Over any field $F$, at any level $\ell\ge1$, with $q_H\ne1$ of finite order
$e\ge2$ and charges $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$, use the actual multipartition-summand
Schur cover and standards of
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]] and
the integer $J_{\lambda\mu}$ of
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]. Let
$\sim_J$ be the equivalence relation on multipartitions generated by
$J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$ or $J_{\mu\lambda}\ne0$. Then
$$\lambda\sim_J\mu\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Delta^\lambda,\Delta^\mu\text{ lie in one Schur block}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S^\lambda,S^\mu\text{ lie in one Hecke block}.$$
For rank $0$ there is the single empty class. No residue-content block
assertion is used as an input.

items.title: Multipartitions with fixed component cores are cyclotomic Jantzen-connected
items.statement:
Under the arbitrary-field finite-$e$ nondegenerate cyclotomic hypotheses of
[[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]], any
two $\ell$-multipartitions of a common rank $n$ with equal componentwise
$e$-cores are $J$-equivalent, even if their component sizes differ. At fixed
component sizes, the full-level coefficient for a change in a single
component equals its level-one coefficient. The proof consumes the actual
same-$e$-core Hecke Specht block theorem for all ranks
([[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]])
rather than a readiness receipt, and imports no Carter-partition
classification.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Jantzen linkage equivalence [F1], the exact $J$ formula [F2],
the level-one identification [F3], the same-core Hecke block theorem [F4],
and the $e$-core/e-weight conventions [F5]–[F7].

[F1] $\lambda\sim_J\mu$ iff the corresponding Schur standards share a block
iff the Murphy Specht modules share a Hecke block, at any level and over any
field in the stated regime
([[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]]).

[F2] The integer $J_{\lambda\mu}$ is the signed sum of
$\nu_\pi(\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal O}(f_x^\lambda)-\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal O}(f_y^\mu))$
over equal-remainder equal-length hook pairs, $0$ unless $\lambda$ strictly
dominates $\mu$, and every foot difference is nonzero in $K$
([[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]).

[F3] At level one the arbitrary-level cyclotomic Hecke algebra is the finite
type-A Hecke algebra
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).

[F4] Two type-A Hecke Specht modules are in the same block exactly when their
labels have the same $e$-core
([[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]]).

[F5] $e$-core, $e$-quotient and $e$-weight of a partition
([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]), with the core independent of the
removal order ([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]])
and the size/weight formula ([[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]]).

[F6] The actual universal signed-conjugate comparison gives $P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})\cong C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)^\theta$, hence $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})^\theta$; $\theta$ is an involutive algebra automorphism whose pullback is exact ([[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The rank $n$, the charges, and the suppliers of [F1]–[F5].

1.1 One component at a time, at level one. Suppose first that the component sizes agree. For a single component $a$ of rank $m$, the actual level-one Hecke algebra is the finite Hecke algebra by [F3]. Its same-core Specht-block clause [F4], together with the level-one case of the Jantzen linkage equivalence [F1], connects any two rank-$m$ partitions with equal $e$-core by level-one Jantzen edges. The exact signed-conjugate bridge is $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})^\theta$, where $\theta(T_i)=-zT_i^{-1}$ and $P$ denotes the ordinary Dipper–James Specht module. If $\lambda,\mu$ have equal $e$-cores, their transposes have the equal transposed cores, so [F4] puts $P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})$ and $P(\mu^{\mathsf T})$ in the same ordinary Hecke block. An algebra automorphism sends primitive central idempotents bijectively to primitive central idempotents; its exact module pullback therefore preserves the equivalence of sharing a block. Applying the SAME $\theta$ to both modules gives the required Murphy block equality and then [F1] gives the level-one Jantzen connection. No untwisted conjugate-dual identity or algebraic-closure assumption is used. The rank $m=0$ case has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem. [F1, F3, F4, F5, F6]

1.2 Equalizing the component weights. If the component weights differ, choose a component whose weight exceeds its target and one whose weight is deficient; a positive-weight component has a removable $e$-hook by its core construction [F5]. For any prescribed foot residue $f$, moving the lowest bead on runner $f-1$ down by $e$ creates an $e$-hook with that foot residue, since its foot residue is the starting beta position plus one; wrap this hook in the deficient component with the same foot residue. The changed components determine the removed and added hook pair uniquely, and in the appropriate dominance orientation their $J$ contribution is one signed valuation with no cancellation; equal foot residues mean the nonzero generic difference is divisible by $t-1$, so the valuation is a positive integer. Nonzero generic foot differences are part of the exact formula [F2], and no unit-difference or characteristic-zero restriction is inserted. Thus the transfer is a Jantzen edge; it lowers the sum of squares of the discrepancies of the component hook weights by at least $2$, so finitely many such transfers equalize the component weights. Every moved $e$-hook preserves its component's core by [F5], and every step preserves the total rank. [F2, F5]

2.1 Fixed component sizes. For two full multipartitions that differ only in component $a$, every contributing equal-remainder hook pair in $J$ lies in $a$: the other components are unchanged on both sides and cancelling hooks between two unchanged components would return the same multipartition. The common residue factor $Q_at^{na}$ is a unit of $\mathcal O$, and replacing it by the level-one factor $Q_at^m$ multiplies each foot difference by a Laurent unit, so the valuation is unchanged and the full-level $J$ coefficient equals the level-one coefficient of [F2]. Inserting the level-one paths of step 1.1 in component $a$ and leaving the other components fixed connects all multipartitions with equal component sizes and the same component cores. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.2 equalize component sizes along Jantzen edges from any starting multipartition, and step 2.1 connects all multipartitions of fixed component sizes with equal component cores. Composing the two finite chains connects any two multipartitions of rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores, proving that they are $J$-equivalent; the fixed-size comparison of coefficients is step 2.1. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

The lemma reduces the multipartition block question to the componentwise
$e$-core data and the level-one Hecke theorem, using the exact level-one to
finite-Hecke identification and the explicit hook transfer between
components. No choice principle is used: all chains and hook moves are
finite and explicitly constructed.

items.title: Cyclotomic multipartitions have equal residue content exactly when Jantzen-connected
items.statement:
Let $F$ be any field, let $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite order $e\ge2$ with
$q_H\ne1$, let $\ell\ge1$ and $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$. For all $\ell$-multipartitions
$\lambda,\mu$ of rank $n\ge0$, the node-residue contents
$$C_i(\lambda)=\#\{(r,s,a)\in[\lambda]:c_a+s-r\equiv i\pmod e\}$$
agree for every $i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ if and only if
$\lambda\sim_J\mu$ for the exact integer Jantzen coefficients of
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]. This
includes arbitrary levels and all field characteristics.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The rank $n$, the charges $c_a$, and the suppliers of [F1]–[F4].

1.1 Necessity. Suppose $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$; then at least one term of its signed integer sum has nonzero valuation, and evaluating that generic foot difference at $t=1$ gives zero, so the two foot eigenvalues coincide and, since $q_H$ has order $e$, their charged foot residues agree. The two hooks have equal length and the same remainder diagram. Along a rim strip, reading from its lowest-left node to its highest-right node increases the content by one at every step, so its residue multiset consists of $h$ consecutive residues starting at its foot; hence the two removed hooks have identical residue counts and $C(\lambda)=C(\mu)$. Transitivity gives the necessity of $C(\lambda)=C(\mu)$ for every $J$-path. [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 Sufficiency setup: cores and lifts. Let $\kappa$ be the componentwise core of a member of the rank-$n$ content class; its size is at most $n$ and congruent to $n$ modulo $e$, and by [F2] all such cores have the same hub and are connected by the prescribed switch sequence. Every intermediate core has size at most $n$ and the same hub, so adding $(n-\text{core size})/e$ $e$-hooks produces a rank-$n$ multipartition of the same content by the equal-hub/equal-size clause of [F2]. [F2, F4]

2.1 The explicit one-hook lift across a core switch. Let $\kappa'$ be obtained from $\kappa$ by the oriented switch in rows $i,j$ and components $a,b$ of [F2], with $\gamma\ge2$, so $|\kappa'|=|\kappa|-eD$ with $D=\gamma-2\ge0$. Write $u=i+et_{ia}$, $v=j+e(t_{ja}+1)$, $v'=j+et_{jb}$, $u'=i+e(t_{ib}+1)$: the switch removes bead $u$ and inserts $v$ in component $a$, and removes $v'$ and inserts $u'$ in component $b$. Put $w=(n-|\kappa|)/e\ge0$, form $\lambda$ from $\kappa$ by moving the lowest bead $u$ of the $i$-runner in component $a$ to $u+ew$ (adding $w$ $e$-hooks on this runner), and form $\mu$ from $\kappa'$ by moving its lowest bead $v$ on the $j$-runner in component $a$ to $v+e(w+D)$. Both have size $n$, the same hub, and by [F2] equal content. Their beta sets in component $a$ differ only by replacing $u+ew$ with $v+e(w+D)$, and those in component $b$ only by replacing $v'$ with $u'$. Because $(v-u)+(u'-v')=-eD$, we have $v+e(w+D)-(u+ew)=v'-u'$, so the two components exchange a single rim hook of length $|v'-u'|$, nonzero since $i\ne j$ modulo $e$. If $v'-u'>0$, component $b$ unwraps and $a$ wraps a hook with foot residue $i+1$ modulo $e$; otherwise $a$ unwraps and $b$ wraps one with foot residue $j+1$. In both cases the hook feet have equal residues, and the hook pair is uniquely determined because distinct components change, so the $J$ coefficient of [F1] is a single signed valuation, a nonzero integer with no cancellation. Hence $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are Jantzen-connected by one edge; this supplies the detail abbreviated in the Lyle–Mathas tight lemma. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

3.1 Termination and conclusion. The generic difference of the unique hook contribution is nonzero by [F1], and its specialization vanishes because the charged feet agree, so its positive integer valuation cannot disappear under reduction modulo $\operatorname{char}F$. The fixed-core lemma [F3] permits replacing arbitrary lifts by the chosen lifts before and after each switch, and strict descent lowers the nonnegative core size by at least $e$, so the process terminates at a minimum core; all minimum cores have equal size and are connected by $\gamma=2$ switches, whose rank-$n$ lifts are connected by the same explicit construction of step 2.1. Together with the fixed-component-size lifts of [F3], every member of the content class is Jantzen-connected to every other, and step 1.1 gives the converse. The empty rank has only one multipartition and is immediate; no affine-center or primitive-block theorem has entered the proof. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Central content sectors are zero or primitive cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement:
Let $F$ be any field and let $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite quantum
characteristic $e\ge2$. Use the standard cyclotomic type-A Hecke presentation
with level $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ge0$ imposed on the first polynomial
variable, with $\lambda_i\ge0$ and $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. For $q_H\ne1$ the
roots are $q_H^i$ and $q_H$ has order $e$; for $q_H=1$ one has
$\operatorname{char}F=e>0$ and the roots are the prime-field residues $i$.
Using the central CRT notation of
[[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]] and
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]], for
every content $\alpha$ of rank $d$ the element
$e_\alpha=\sum_{\text{word content }\alpha}e(\text{word})$ is either zero or a
primitive central idempotent. The nonzero $e_\alpha$ are exactly all
primitive central idempotents, so $H_d^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha
e_\alpha H_d^\Lambda$ is precisely the block decomposition. At $d=0$ the
unique sector is $F$, regardless of level; at $d>0$, $\ell=0$ the algebra is
zero. This is an arbitrary-level result over the original field in both
branches.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The field $F$, the finite quantum characteristic $e$, the

multiplicities $\lambda_i$, and the suppliers of [F1]–[F8].

1.1 Base cases. At rank $0$ the algebra is $F$, the empty-word projector is $1$, and this is its unique primitive central idempotent. At positive rank and level $0$ the defining polynomial is $1$, so the algebra is $0$ and every content sector is $0$, with no nonzero blocks. Hence assume rank $d\ge1$ and level $\ell\ge1$. [F1]

1.2 The degenerate branch. In the branch $q_H=1$ necessarily $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$. The center is the full symmetric-polynomial image over this $F$ by [F3], and [F4] applies to the early CRT projectors and proves that their content sums are zero or primitive. This uses neither a field extension nor a power-sum generation assertion. [F1, F3, F4]

1.3 The nondegenerate branch: labels of sectors. In the branch $q_H\ne1$ choose a charge list $c_1,\dots,c_\ell$ repeating each $i$ exactly $\lambda_i$ times, so $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$ and the first polynomial is unchanged. The arbitrary-level Murphy cellular basis and the finite cellular head lemma [F5] supply all simple $H_d^\Lambda$-modules as nonzero Specht quotients $D^\lambda$, and the content-triangular JM action [F6] says every word on $S^\lambda$, hence on $D^\lambda$, has the node content $C(\lambda)$. Thus a simple module lying in a nonzero sector $e_\alpha$ has a label $\lambda$ with $C(\lambda)=\alpha$. [F1, F5, F6]

2.1 Primitivity of the nonzero sectors. Any two simple modules in the sector $e_\alpha$ have labels with equal content, so [F7] connects the labels by integer Jantzen edges and [F8] transfers this to a common Hecke block. If $e_\alpha$ decomposed into two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents $u,v$, the nonzero finite algebras $uH_d^\Lambda$ and $vH_d^\Lambda$ would each have a simple module, obtained from a proper right ideal of maximal dimension. Those simple modules cannot lie in one block, because the central idempotent $u$ acts as the identity on the first and as zero on the second, and all modules and extensions split by $u$. This contradicts the one-block assertion, so $e_\alpha$ is primitive. [F1, F7, F8, step 1.3]

3.1 Every block is a content sector. In either branch let $b$ be a primitive central idempotent and write $b=\sum_\alpha be_\alpha$. The terms are central orthogonal idempotents, so precisely one is nonzero and $b=be_\alpha$; primitivity of the nonzero $e_\alpha$ from step 1.2 or step 2.1 gives $b=e_\alpha$. Hence the nonzero content sums are exactly all primitive central idempotents and the decomposition $H_d^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha e_\alpha H_d^\Lambda$ is precisely the block decomposition [F2]. All sums are finite, the field characteristic never reduces an integer $K_0$ adjacency, and no affine-block classification or citation-only center theorem is consumed. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Residue-sequence idempotents and cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement:
Work in the charged finite-$e$ field conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. By
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]],
$H^\Lambda_d$ is finite-dimensional and each minimal polynomial of the
polynomial generator $z_r=X_r$ (nondegenerate normalization) respectively
$x_r$ (degenerate normalization) splits over the residues $c_i=q_H^i$
respectively $i\cdot1_F$.

**Residue-sequence idempotents.** Let $\varepsilon_r(i)$ be the canonical CRT
primary idempotent of that generator at the spectral value $c_i$ associated with residue label $i$ (zero when that value is
absent), and put
$$e(\nu)=\prod_{r=1}^{d}\varepsilon_r(\nu_r)$$
for a residue sequence $\nu=(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_d)\in(\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z)^d$. On
every finite $H$-module the element $e(\nu)$ projects onto the joint
generalized residue space, and these mutually orthogonal idempotents sum to
$1$. At content $\alpha$ put
$$e_\alpha=\sum_{\nu\in I_\alpha}e(\nu),$$
the sum over residue sequences of content $\alpha$; it is central, and
$H^\Lambda_d$ is the direct sum of its central ideals
$$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d\,e_\alpha.$$
By
[[thm-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sectors-are-zero-or-primitive-blocks]],
every nonzero $e_\alpha$ is primitive, so every nonzero $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
an actual block
([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
this block assertion is proved there, not retained as an unused citation.
The algebra basis and dimension convention is that of
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra-basis-and-dimension]].

**Level one.** At level one, $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the polynomial generators
correspond under the explicit finite-Hecke inverse of
[[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]] to
$$X_r=q_H^j\bigl(1+(q_H-1)L_r\bigr)\quad\text{(nondegenerate)},\qquad x_r=j+L_r\quad\text{(degenerate)},$$
where $L_r$ is the ordinary additive Jucys–Murphy element. Thus on a standard
tableau node of content $m$ their eigenvalues are $q_H^{j+m}$ respectively
$j+m$, while $L_r$ itself has additive $q$-content $[m]_{q_H}$. The nonzero
joint projectors are precisely the residue words of standard tableaux
([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]), and grouping
those words by content gives the block labels.

**Boundary conventions.** At rank zero the empty projector is $1$ and the
unique block is $F$; at level zero and positive rank all projectors and blocks
are zero. The projection, centrality, and block-decomposition assertions
recorded here are exactly the proved content-sector statements of the linked
suppliers; this definition introduces no new primitive-block classification
of its own. It uses no choice principle: all spectra, projectors, and sums are
finite.
items.strategy: Finite/split spectrum and CRT sums are the declared early lemma, proved independently of basis independence and primitivity by direct global intertwiners and determinant/adjugate annihilators. The separately declared unified primitivity theorem supplies both arbitrary-field branches: NG uses actual Schur/Jantzen/core connectivity, DG uses the proved symmetric-JM center and nilpotent augmentation argument. The level-one JM formulas follow from the independently constructed inverse, with the factor q_H^j and the additive-versus-multiplicative distinction explicit. The ordinary JM cell action is triangular on every field. Filtering the regular algebra by its Murphy cell layers shows a word projector is nonzero exactly when it occurs on a standard-tableau word: the primary-projector functor is exact, each cell layer is the corresponding cell module tensor its finite free left-index space, and every diagonal word occurs in that cell module's finite triangular filtration. This does not require semisimplicity or nonzero cell heads. Every retained block/eigenvalue claim therefore has an actual local supplier; the primitive theorem never supplies its own early CRT/BK prerequisites.

items.title: The Brundan–Kleshchev blockwise Hecke–KLR isomorphism
items.statement:
Let $F$ be any field, let $q\in F^\times$ have finite quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)\ge2$, let $\Lambda\in P^+$ be dominant and let $\alpha\in Q_+$ have
height $d$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, in the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] and
[[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]. Then the
homomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and
$\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually
inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
generated by the Khovanov–Lauda generators
$\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations
(1.6)–(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalized by
$\rho(e(i))=e(i)$ and
$$\rho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)\quad(q\ne1),\qquad \rho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)\quad(q=1).$$
The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate
($q\ne1$) cases are proved separately, and both hold in finite quantum
characteristic $e$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The field $F$, the finite quantum characteristic $e$, the dominant

weight $\Lambda$, the content $\alpha$ of height $d$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, and

the suppliers of [F1]–[F4].

1.1 The mutually inverse early maps. By [F3] the local KLR generators of the nonzero sector satisfy the KLR relations, so there is a unique algebra homomorphism $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ sending $e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $y_r\mapsto y_r$ and $\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$; by [F4] the Hecke generators $X_r,T_r$ (respectively $x_r,s_r$) of the sector satisfy the affine Hecke and cyclotomic relations, so there is a unique homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\sigma(e(i))=e(i)$ for $i\in I_\alpha$. The early central sector isomorphism [F2] proves, by explicit generator composites that are literally the identity, that $\rho$ and $\sigma$ are mutually inverse over $F$ for every content, including the zero sectors, with $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if and only if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$. No algebraic closure, root extraction, dimension argument or primitive-block premise was used to construct these maps. [F2, F3, F4]

1.2 Primitivity of the sector. By [F1] every nonzero $e_\alpha$ is primitive and every nonzero $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is an actual block. Hence for the content $\alpha$ of the Statement the sector $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a block of $H^\Lambda_d$, and the block terminology in the Statement is justified rather than assumed. [F1]

2.1 The blockwise isomorphism and its normalization. Restricting the mutually inverse maps of step 1.1 to the nonzero sector $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ gives mutually inverse unital $F$-algebra isomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. The defining formulas of $\rho$ give $\rho(e(i))=e(i)$ and the stated dot normalization $\rho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ in the nondegenerate case and $\rho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ in the degenerate case, matching the dot images of [F2]. Because $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the algebra generated by $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the defining KLR relations and $\rho$ is an isomorphism, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is generated by the images of those generators subject only to those relations. The degenerate and nondegenerate cases were proved separately by [F2]–[F4] and both hold in finite quantum characteristic $e$, with no characteristic-zero or level-one restriction. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke blocks inherit a nontrivial Z-grading
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], each fixed choice
of admissible local normalising series transports the KLR homogeneous
decomposition to a $\mathbb Z$-grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. This is the
unique grading for those fixed generator images with $\deg e(i)=0$,
$\deg y_r=2$ and
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Different admissible
series choices give graded-isomorphic transported algebras via
$\rho'\circ\rho^{-1}$; their underlying identity map need not be graded. The
grading can be nontrivial, but it may be trivial on an individual block,
including the one-dimensional level-one rank-two $e=3$ blocks. The ordinary
Hecke presentation always has the trivial assignment of degree zero to all
its generators; the transported grading is generally expressed using the
nilpotent dots and local crossings, and ordinary Hecke generators can be sums
of different homogeneous pieces and may be homogeneous in special cases. No
claim forbids the degree-zero assignment or asserts that every block grading
is nontrivial.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The field $F$, the finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$, the

dominant weight $\Lambda$, and the suppliers of [F1]–[F3].

1.1 Transport of the grading. Fix a choice of admissible local normalising series, hence the isomorphism $\rho$ of [F1]. Declare each image of a homogeneous KLR generator to be homogeneous of the same degree; the images generate $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ and the KLR relations of [F2] are homogeneous, so the resulting degree assignment is well defined. Products retain degree addition because $\rho$ is an algebra map, so the degree summands are exactly the transported homogeneous summands. Since the generator images span the algebra, their assigned degrees determine every degree summand and give uniqueness of the grading for that fixed choice, with $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Independence of the series choice. If $\rho'$ is the isomorphism attached to another admissible series, then $\rho'\circ\rho^{-1}$ sends each homogeneous native generator image of the first choice to the corresponding new image and hence is graded by construction; the two transported algebras are graded-isomorphic, while the underlying identity map on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ need not be graded because the two series differ by units that need not be homogeneous of degree zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

2.2 Triviality is not excluded. Assigning degree zero to every ordinary Hecke generator makes all defining relations homogeneous, so the degree-zero assignment is a legitimate grading of the ordinary Hecke presentation and no impossibility statement is asserted. A one-dimensional sector has only degree zero, because its unit has degree zero and it equals $F$; in particular the one-dimensional level-one rank-two $e=3$ blocks are trivially graded. [F1, step 1.1]

2.3 A concrete nontrivial witness. Consider level one, $e=2$, rank two. Of the four colour words only $(0,1)$ survives: the first-strand exponent zero kills $(1,0)$, and on $(0,0)$ the equal-colour mixed identities give $\psi_1y_2=1$ together with $\psi_1^2=0$, hence $\psi_1=0$ after left multiplication by $\psi_1$, giving $1=0$; so the equal-colour sector is zero, with $y_1=0$ and the crossing zero. The quadratic double-edge relation gives $y_2^2=0$. Conversely $e(0,1)=1$, $y_2=t$, $y_1=\psi_1=0$ in $F[t]/(t^2)$ satisfy all rank-two relations, so that sector is $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg t=2$, and its Brundan–Kleshchev image supplies an actual nontrivial transported grading, including in the characteristic-two degeneration. This is a witness that the construction can be nontrivial, not a claim about all sectors. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Conclusion. Each fixed admissible series choice transports the KLR homogeneous decomposition to a $\mathbb Z$-grading of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$, unique for the induced generator degrees; different choices give graded-isomorphic transported algebras; and the grading may be nontrivial on some blocks while trivial on others, with the ordinary presentation retaining its degree-zero assignment. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.3] ∎

items.title: Homogeneous degree check for the corrected KLR braid relation
items.statement: In the specialized cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the grading $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$, fix a triple $i=(i_r,i_{r+1},i_{r+2})$ and put $d(i):=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}-a_{i_ri_{r+2}}-a_{i_{r+1}i_{r+2}}$ (the degree of both three-crossing words $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_re(i)$ and $\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}e(i)$, computed on the successive permuted colour pairs). Then both sides of (1.15) are homogeneous of degree $d(i)$ and the correction term has the same degree: it is $\pm1$ (degree $0$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\to i_{r+1}$ or $i_{r+2}=i_r\leftarrow i_{r+1}$, it is $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ (degree $2$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\rightleftarrows i_{r+1}$ (the $e=2$ double edge), and it is $0$ otherwise. In particular the single-edge corrected braid relations have degree $0$ and the $e=2$ double-edge corrected braid relation has degree $2$; both match the two sides.
items.strategy: Substitute the cyclic Cartan entries ($a_{mm}=2$, $a_{m,m\pm1}=-1$ for $e\ge3$, $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ for $e=2$) into the degree of the words: the three crossings of $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_re(i)$ cross the colour pairs $(i_r,i_{r+1})$, $(i_r,i_{r+2})$, $(i_{r+1},i_{r+2})$ of the successive permuted sequences, so the degree is the displayed $d(i)$; the other braid word has the same multiset of pairs. Case check: (a) $i_{r+2}=i_r\to i_{r+1}$: $d(i)=-(-1)-2-(-1)=0$ and the correction is $+1$; (b) $i_{r+2}=i_r\leftarrow i_{r+1}$: $d(i)=0$ and the correction is $-1$; (c) $e=2$, $i_{r+2}=i_r\rightleftarrows i_{r+1}$: $a_{i_ri_{r+1}}=a_{i_{r+1}i_{r+2}}=-2$, $a_{i_ri_{r+2}}=a_{00}=2$, so $d(i)=2+2-2=2$, matching the degree $2$ of $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$; (d) all other cases have correction $0$. The degrees are those of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], and the case list is the source's (1.15). No choice is used. The displayed source word order is ψ_rψ_(r+1)ψ_r−ψ_(r+1)ψ_rψ_(r+1); it equals the native opposite-order τ difference under ψ=−τ. The nonzero correction requires equal outer colors; zero corrections remain homogeneous without asserting their degree is zero.

items.title: The degenerate level-one Hecke–KLR map for S_3
items.statement: Work over $F=\mathbb F_3$ with $q=1$ (so $e=3$), $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one) and $d=3$: then $H^\Lambda_3\cong \mathbb F_3S_3$ and exactly one block is nonzero, namely $\alpha=\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ with $e_\alpha=1$. The residue sequences realised by standard tableaux all have residue multiset $\{0,1,2\}$. The degenerate KLR generators are the elements $y_r=\sum_i(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ with $x_r$ the Jucys-Murphy elements of $\mathbb F_3S_3$ (so $x_1=0$, $x_2=(12)$, $x_3=(13)+(23)$), and $\psi_r=\sum_i\varphi_rq_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$ with $\varphi_r=s_r+p_r(i)$ and $p_r(i)=(i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1}$ on unequal components. In this block the mixed relations $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)+e(i)$ for $i_1=i_2$ and $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)$ for $i_1\ne i_2$, and the quadratic relation $\psi_1^2e(i)=(y_2-y_1)e(i)$ for $i_1\to i_2$, are explicit identities in the six-dimensional algebra $\mathbb F_3S_3$.
items.strategy:
Let c=(12), s=(23), a=(13), and C=c+a+s in F_3S_3. Group multiplication gives C²=0 and Cc=Cs=1+(123)+(132). Put e_+=(1+c)/2 and e_-=(1−c)/2 (2 is invertible in F_3). These are the actual joint CRT projectors e(0,1,2),e(0,2,1): x_1=0,x_2=c,x_3=C−c, so y_1=y_2=0 and y_3=C. All other words vanish. Both projectors are nonzero by the group basis. The full center has basis1,C,1+(123)+(132), with square-zero augmentation ideal spanned by the last two elements; hence it has no nontrivial idempotent and there is one block. This also follows from the declared primitive-content theorem.
For the explicit source3.30 choices, ψ_1=0. On e_+, p_2=−1+C and q_2=−1; on e_-, p_2=1+C and q_2=1. Thus ψ_2e_+=(1−s−C)e_+ and ψ_2e_-=(s+1+C)e_-. Direct group multiplication, c²=s²=1 and csc=scs give ψ_2e_+=e_-ψ_2, ψ_2e_-=e_+ψ_2, ψ_2²e_+=Ce_+, ψ_2²e_-=−Ce_-, and Cψ_2=ψ_2C=0. These are the claimed mixed and quadratic identities with y_3=C,y_2=0. First-crossing mixed identities are zero on every surviving unequal-color word; equal-first-color words are absent, so the universal equal-color formula also holds. The explicit six group elements give the dimension6; no primitive-block citation or Hecke-basis dimension loop is hidden.

items.statement:
Let $F$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $
e3$, let $q\in F^{	imes}$ be a primitive cube root of unity (so $e=3$), $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one) and $d=2$. Then: (i) for $i=(i_1,i_2)\in I^2$ the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; thus $y_1e(i)=0$ for the three sequences with $i_1=0$, and $e(i)=0$ for all six sequences with $i_1
e0$, because their exponent is zero and $y_1^0e(i)=e(i)$; (ii) $\psi_1^2e(i)$ equals $0$ if $i_1=i_2$, equals $(y_2-y_1)e(i)$ if $i_2=i_1+1$ and equals $(y_1-y_2)e(i)$ if $i_2=i_1-1$; for $e=3$ these are all cases; (iii) the nonzero blocks of $H^\Lambda_2$ are exactly $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$; both are one dimensional, with $e((0,1))
e0$ in the first (the block of the trivial module of $H_{F,q}(S_2)$) and $e((0,2))
e0$ in the second (the block of the sign module); the other four $\alpha$-blocks of height $2$ are zero.
items.strategy:
Enumerate $I^2=\{0,1,2\}^2$ and apply [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]: the cyclotomic exponent is $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_{i_1})=\delta_{i_1,0}$, giving (i): exponent zero kills the idempotent, not merely a degree-one dot relation, and the quadratic case distinction (1.14) with all adjacent pairs in the 3-cycle gives (ii). For (iii): the independent level-one isomorphism and finite standard basis {1,T_1} give dimension2, and [[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]] identifies $H^\Lambda_2$ with $H_{F,q}(S_2)\cong F[T]/(T^2-(q-1)T-q)=F[T]/((T-q)(T+1))\cong F	imes F$ (distinct roots because $q
e1$ and $q
e-1$ for a primitive cube root in characteristic $
e3$). Hence there are exactly two nonzero one-dimensional blocks, and their labels are computed from the polynomial generator: on the trivial module $X_1=q^0=1$ and $X_2=q^{-1}T_1X_1T_1=q^{-1}q^2=q$, giving residue sequence $(0,1)$; on the sign module $X_1=1$ and $X_2=q^{-1}(-1)^2=q^{-1}=q^2$, giving $(0,2)$ - equivalently the q-contents of the standard tableaux of $(2)$ and $(1,1)$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]). Every nonzero block contains at least one such idempotent, so the remaining four are zero. No choice is used.

items.title: The whole affine Hecke algebra is not one cyclotomic KLR block
items.statement: For a fixed content-block isomorphism, replacing one side by the whole affine algebra, or by the whole cyclotomic quotient in the example below, fails. This does not forbid summing all the central-sector isomorphisms on BOTH sides: (i) the affine Hecke algebra $H_1$ is $F[x_1^{\pm1}]$ resp. $F[x_1]$, hence infinite dimensional, while every cyclotomic block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite dimensional of dimension $\le\ell^dd!$; (ii) even after imposing the cyclotomic relation, a single residue-content idempotent $e_\alpha$ cuts out a proper factor: at level one with $d=2$, $e=3$ and $q$ a primitive cube root, $H^\Lambda_2\cong H_{F,q}(S_2)\cong F\times F$ has two nonzero blocks $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$, so $H^\Lambda_2$ is not isomorphic to either one of them, and on the KLR side $R^\Lambda_2=R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}\oplus R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$ is not isomorphic to a single block.
items.strategy: At rankone the affine presentation is the Laurent polynomial ring F[X_1^(±1)] in NG and polynomial ring F[x_1] in DG. Distinct powers are linearly independent, so each is infinite-dimensional. Charged cyclotomic quotients and their sectors are finite by the independent bounded spanning lemma (and later exact basis). For the stated levelone ranktwo e3 example the explicit JM inverse identifies H with F[T]/((T−q_H)(T+1)); q_H and −1 are distinct, so CRT gives F×F. The two normalized spectral sequences are (0,1),(0,2), as computed in the actual example. Hence each primitive block is F, whereas the whole quotient has dimension2, and its early BK image is the direct sum of the corresponding two KLR algebras. This proves both counterexample branches with the actual field/generator normalization.
